context:
Goal: the Stop hook refuses to end a turn with an open CI wait and no check-in, without false alarms or misses.
Problem (rule): the hook keeps ONE wait, the newest ready call. Ready PR 5, then ready PR 6, then a CI green line that names no PR: the wait closes, PR 5 has no check-in, and Stop passes. Only you can say which loss is worth the cost: a miss on an older PR (a), or a new rule for a green line with no PR (b).
Based on (code, lane's read, unchecked by triage): hooks/stall_watch.py `open_ci_wait`; reviewer round 1 probe on #3410.
Based on (ruling): own-ci-wait-subscribe-guard (owner 21:39 CST Nov 13, relayed): a session should subscribe or poll to be woken; check-ins are the safety net. It says nothing on one wait versus many.
Departs from: main — it has no CI-wait check at all; the lane adds one wait (a) or one wait per ready PR (b).
Meanwhile: the lane keeps this as a recorded Limit in decision ci-wait-reads-run-status and does not wait for you.
Option a is starred at the lane's recommendation (simpler: a green line cannot tell which PR it means). Neither option widens what a shared tool accepts.
Your question, 15:01 CST Nov 14: "which is best to prioritize speed?" Triage's answer (unmeasured; neither option was timed): option a is the cheaper change and the one the lane recommends; the check stays one line, and nothing new is written or tested. Option b costs a new rule (a green line with no PR closes all waits or none) and its tests, and gains that no ready PR goes unchecked. Per the coordinator's 14:42 CST report, runner 10 now sets a check-in on each ready mark by hand, which covers the older PR that option a leaves open. Your pick; the star on a stays the lane's recommendation, not triage's.
Your question, 18:37 CST Nov 14: "is B better". Triage's answer (a reading, not a measure; you have not picked): b is better at the outcome, a is better at cost. b leaves no ready PR without a check-in; a can leave an older one uncovered while Stop passes. b's price is one new rule (a green line with no PR closes all waits or none) and its tests. Not measured: how often a session has two ready PRs at once. What covers a today: runner 10 sets a check-in on each ready mark by hand (coordinator's 14:42 CST report, not read by triage). Only the lane recommends, and it recommends a; no session recommends b, so the star stays on a. The coordinator is asked for its view on b. Nothing waits.
Update 18:43 CST Nov 14: Source: coordinator's Explore read (read-only Sonnet agent, hooks/stall_watch.py, hooks/guard.py and step ci-wait-stop-needs-checkin at local main af2c312c, shallow, later edits unknown); unverified by triage; the coordinator did not read this item's text. The lane recommended a earlier. The coordinator now recommends b (its own pick, undoable). b widens nothing: it makes the check stricter. Its gain: after ready PR 5, ready PR 6, then a green line naming no PR, PR 5 still needs its check-in, so no PR is left without a wake; the case is real: two ready runs were in CI at once (#3424 and #3425, 18:02 to 18:15 CST Nov 14, n=1). Its cost: one new rule and its tests, and a Stop that blocks more often. The star moves from a to b at the coordinator's named recommendation; the lane's a is unstarred. Stop check, coordinator's Explore read, unverified by triage: it counts send_later, create_trigger, CronCreate and ScheduleWakeup as a check-in (stall_watch.py:862, tests CI03-CI06). It reads only the tool name (:975), never run_once_at, cron_expression or recurring, so a recurring check-in passes; only the remedy text says one-time. It reads the transcript only and keeps ONE wait, the newest ready call. The 55-minute cap (guard.py, ci_wait_cap.json) guards only send_later with CI wording. Cost: no new process, file or timer. Usage by sessions is unmeasured except list_triggers at 18:41 CST Nov 14: 2 one-shot, 0 recurring, both runner 10's check-ins. Your pick. Nothing waits.
CLOSED 20:20 CST Nov 14 on the COORDINATOR'S pick, option b (one wait per ready PR), taken under the owner's 20:18 CST Nov 14 words ("Nothing can't be undone don't wait on me") (owner words relayed by the consultant 20:20; the pick is the coordinator's, undoable, not the owner's own). Ruling coord-836-b-one-wait-per-ready-pr. If you disagree, say so and it reopens.

short: When a session waits on two ready PRs, does the Stop check hold one wait or one per PR?
title: When a session has marked two PRs ready, does the Stop check keep one wait, the newest (a), or one wait per ready PR (b)?
why: The check keeps one wait today. A green line names no PR, so one line can close the wait while an older ready PR has no check-in, and Stop then passes.
